learning_outcomes.text: Analyze simple or complex electronic circuits
Implement electronic circuits and measure their characteristics
Verify the correct operation of a given circuit

syllabus_topics: Field effect transistors and bipolar junction transistors: a) physical structure and operation, b) current-voltage characteristics, c) DC operation - bias, d) small-signal equivalent circuit models
Single-stage transistor based amplifier topologies: biasing and operation
teaching_methods: Use of e-slides and interactive board during lectures
Use of computer-aided design tools at the laboratory (circuit design and simulation)
Use of components and instruments (signal generators, power supplies, multi-meters, oscilloscopes) at the laboratory for circuit implementation and measurement
Use of email for information exchange

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory exercises and final examination at the laboratory

assessment_rules: The final examination, which includes problem solving, accounts for 80% of the grade, evaluated based on the correctness and completeness of answers. Laboratory exercises on circuit design, simulation, implementation and measurement, including a final laboratory examination, account for 20%. Home-works on problem solving can provide a bonus of up to 10% in case of successful evaluation in the final exam and lab exercises. The evaluation procedure is accessible via the course website.
bibliography: MICROELECTRONICS, Richard Jaeger and Travis Blalock, 5th edition, McGraw-Hill, 2018.
FUNDAMENTALS OF MICROELECTRONICS, 2nd edition, John Wiley & Sons, BEHZAD RAZAVI, 2018.
Transactions on Circuits and Systems I & II (TCAS), IEEE.
degree: Computer Science and Engineering (Diploma, 4 years / 240 ECTS, undergraduate programme)
